false_positive_rejection_rules.description: Reject ordinary paragraph prose that pdf_oxide split into fake table rows/cells.
reject_when_all_supported: visible region has no grid lines or cell boundaries
visible region has no semantic row-column relationship
candidate rows read as continuous paragraph prose fragments
candidate has one populated prose column plus empty trailing cells
correction_contract: Use replace_element only when paragraph_block is persistable downstream.
Preserve source_bbox when it tightly covers the prose excerpt.
Do not reconstruct body_text from corrupted fake table cells in this pass.
false_positive_rejection_rules.positive_control: Do not apply this rejection rule to real tables with explicit header-row evidence and populated data rows.

false_positive_rejection_rules.description: Reject titled bordered or shaded prose callouts that pdf_oxide promoted to tables.
reject_when_all_supported: visible region is bordered or shaded
visible region has a title plus prose body
visible region has no table grid, column headers, or structured rows
correction_contract: Emit corrected_bbox for the outer visible callout when source_bbox is over_broad.
Route to pdf.boxed_callout.v1 when boxed_callout is not persistable downstream.

merge_review_contract.purpose: Decide whether visually adjacent table candidates should remain separate tables or merge into one logical table.
merge_review_contract.decision_rule: Use both annotated page images and extracted table metrics. Merge only when visual continuity, compatible column structure, and cell/data quality support one logical table; otherwise classify as separate tables or engineering backlog.
merge_review_contract.human_triage_gate: Escalate only when the supplied images and metrics conflict on whether adjacent table regions are one logical table and the selected preset validators cannot resolve it.

human_triage_gate: Only escalate when visible table content and actual/candidate JSON conflict on table identity, bounds, merge/continuation status, row structure, column structure, spanning cells, or cell text.
